categories.main_business_segments: SUMCO operates a single business segment: the manufacturing and sale of high-purity silicon wafers for semiconductor manufacturers. These wafers serve as the substrate material for a wide range of semiconductor devices, including memory and logic chips.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company’s core technologies include the growth of high-purity single crystal silicon ingots using advanced crystal pulling (Czochralski) methods, followed by precision wafer slicing, grinding, polishing, and cleaning. SUMCO also produces epitaxial wafers by depositing thin silicon layers on polished wafers to enhance surface quality, and leverages AI for productivity improvements.
categories.primary_customers_markets: SUMCO’s primary customers are major global semiconductor manufacturers. Its wafers are used in semiconductors for data centers, consumer electronics, automotive (including EV/HEV), industrial, and communications applications. The company’s sales are highly concentrated, with a significant portion to large trading companies and leading device makers.
categories.geographic_coverage: SUMCO has manufacturing and sales operations in Japan, Taiwan, the United States, Indonesia, and Singapore, with sales offices in Japan, the US, Europe (UK), Taiwan, Singapore, and technical support in Taiwan and Korea. Its customer base is global, with significant sales in Japan, Taiwan, China, the US, Korea, and Europe.
categories.supply_chain_position: SUMCO is positioned midstream in the semiconductor supply chain, supplying silicon wafers as essential substrates to downstream semiconductor device manufacturers. It procures high-purity polysilicon upstream and delivers processed wafers to chipmakers.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategically, SUMCO focuses on maintaining technological leadership in large-diameter (300mm) advanced wafers, responding to AI-driven and automotive semiconductor demand, and modernizing production facilities. R&D priorities include next-generation wafer technologies, high value-added products (e.g., epitaxial wafers), productivity improvements via AI, and sustainability initiatives such as carbon neutrality.
categories.revenue_model: SUMCO generates revenue primarily through the sale of silicon wafers to semiconductor manufacturers, with most transactions based on direct sales contracts, including some long-term agreements. Revenue is recognized upon delivery or customer acceptance of the wafers.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: SUMCO is one of the world’s leading silicon wafer suppliers, competing globally with companies such as Shin-Etsu Handotai (SEH), GlobalWafers, Siltronic, and SK Siltron. The industry is highly concentrated, with a few large players dominating the market; SUMCO holds a strong position, especially in advanced 300mm wafers.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In FY2024, SUMCO reported consolidated net sales of 396.6 billion yen, operating profit of 36.9 billion yen, and net income attributable to shareholders of 19.9 billion yen. The company employs approximately 9,850 people. After a period of strong growth through 2022, recent years have seen a sales and profit decline due to market adjustments, but the company continues to invest heavily in capacity and technology for future growth.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: SUMCO emphasizes its ability to deliver high-quality, high-purity silicon wafers with advanced specifications, supporting the miniaturization and performance requirements of next-generation semiconductors. Its differentiation lies in technological expertise, broad product lineup (from small to large diameters), stable global supply, and close collaboration with leading semiconductor manufacturers.
